notes: Coder A's per-unit 'why' fields were written after coding (disclosed in A's notes) and were ignored; every disagreement was settled by re-reading the saved source text, and no unit rationales were added to v2/inst (validated with --no-why). Units were aligned by anchor/sentence overlap; no hand re-pairing was needed. Stance agreed on all 6 documents. PATTERN 1, phase of P10 'ask your instructor if unsure' units (5 of the phase disagreements: CS honesty, tiers translation-tools note, CS 51, CS 62, CS 105): A during-work, B course-start -> course-start, matching the GT/UCI rule for clarification-seeking units and the agreed Tier 1 'read the syllabus and discuss allowed uses' unit. Handbook 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' -> during-work (A): it names conduct forbidden in independently prepared work, not a sanction; B's normalized text (an example of representing others' ideas as one's own) was kept as more faithful. PATTERN 2, modality. Consequence statements 'If a student uses AI in a way that does not align with the tier system ... it is considered a violation' (tiers page and CS honesty page) -> informs (B), as in GT; the rule itself is carried by the tier units. Literal 'should' in CS 62 -> should-not for 'AI tools should not be used on the assignments ... in any way' and the generate/debug parenthetical (B); the VS Code sentence 'You should be writing all of your code on your own without any additional tools beyond VS Code (without AI tools installed)' -> split into should (write your own code, only-A kept) and should-not (no extra tools or AI in VS Code), since one sentence holds two rules. CS 105 'In general, you are to use your professor and TAs as the primary resource ... rather than AI tools' -> must ('are to' is directive; 'in general' kept in the text). Staff procedures -> must: 'uses a clear and convincing standard' (binding on the Board), 'We routinely use software ... to detect similarities' (a standing detection commitment, matching the UIUC 'We will run automated checks' resolution). CS honesty 'Any exceptions or differences will appear in the course syllabus or the instructions for an assignment' -> must (a 'will' commitment) with type P04 (course- and assignment-level variation; P09 would require an AI statement in every syllabus, which this does not say). PATTERN 3, policy_type. Tier 0 disallowed-uses list (tiers page and CS 105) -> P01 (B): it spells out the full ban, including non-submission uses such as study guides, which P19 does not cover. Tiers purpose and 'general usage rather than specific tools' -> P56 (a preamble stating purpose and scope). Tier 3 'treated as the student's own work' -> P29 (B); P28 concerns disclosure. CS 105 rationale 'ensure that your out-of-class help is targeted towards your learning' -> actor student (it addresses 'you'). PATTERN 4, merged vs split. B split the Tier 0 Grammarly exclusion ('not tools that offer suggested revisions') and the Tier 3 'do not need to credit their use' out of A's merged units; kept B's splits (one rule per unit; the no-credit unit set to may, since it releases students from disclosure) and used B's text for the matched units. Same split kept in CS 105. CS honesty: kept only-B 'the Department will recommend a failing grade' (A had merged it into the second-offense unit, whose final text is now the anchor alone), used B's text for the citation unit (A's merged the prose-ownership rule, which has its own unit), kept only-A 'Your learning is compromised when you violate this principle' (P41 rationale for independent work that includes AI tools), dropped only-A 'Each examination will have a clear statement of what resources are permitted' (no AI or tool reference; A also merged two sentences). Handbook: kept only-B 'All charges must be brought within ten (10) academic days' and the hearing-panel referral note (actor set to admin, since referral happens in the Vice-President's preliminary process); dropped only-A 'students never intentionally represent the ideas or the language of others as their own', because it is the same sentence and rule as the agreed AI unit, whose B text states it. CS 51: dropped only-A general external-source ban, because the next sentence ('This includes AI tools') is the same rule, and the matched unit uses B's merged text. CS 105: dropped only-A 'revise your writing, or check your work' (an item inside the agreed disallowed-uses list unit). No NEW types were proposed for Pomona.
